title: world_interview/1 — the NEXT question worth asking about a brief, or nothing. One question at a time, because the answer to one changes what is worth asking next; asking several at once is bewildering. The seat must never ask what the brief already answers, and must never ask a question whose only purpose is to fill a slot a world 'usually' has (GA-2/GA-3): the questions come from THIS brief's gaps or they do not come at all. Options are concrete and drawn from the brief; exactly one may be marked recommended so the user can move without deliberating. Free text is always available on the surface and is never enumerated here.

done.description: true when nothing is genuinely undetermined any more. Saying true early is correct and preferable to padding: an interview that asks a question it does not need has taught the user that their answers do not matter.

question.description: The question, in plain language and in the world's own terms. Never engine vocabulary, never a genre's vocabulary.

why.description: One short line on what this changes about the world, so the user knows why they are being asked. Shown under the question.

options.description: Concrete answers drawn from this brief — never generic ('yes'/'no'/'other'). The surface always offers free text alongside these, so these do not need to be exhaustive; they need to be good.

label.description: The answer as the user would say it.

implication.description: What choosing this would make true about the world.

recommended.description: Mark at most one. The default that fits the brief best — the way out for a user who does not want to decide.
